subject.title: [Bug]: browser upload/file chooser flow is flaky and can misreport stale-click failures as browser control timeouts

question: Should Browser upload keep paths-only arm-then-later-click as a supported API, or should agent/tool flows be moved toward atomic upload-with-trigger behavior for dynamic pages?
rationale: Both behaviors are currently supported and shipped, so reliability changes may affect callers that intentionally arm a chooser before a later trigger.

options.title: Prefer atomic without breaking paths-only
options.body: Keep paths-only arming supported, but update agent/tool guidance, timeout handling, and tests so chooser-trigger uploads prefer the existing same-request ref/input path where possible.

options.title: Retire paths-only arming
options.body: Require a trigger ref/inputRef/element or direct input target for uploads and provide migration guidance for callers using delayed chooser arming.

options.title: Document current limitations
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document stale-ref recovery plus selector/batch mitigations, accepting that the underlying flake remains possible.

recommendation.title: Prefer atomic without breaking paths-only
recommendation.body: Keep paths-only arming supported, but update agent/tool guidance, timeout handling, and tests so chooser-trigger uploads prefer the existing same-request ref/input path where possible.
